title: Four Directions for the Jam
body:
I have been pushing “charge” in four different directions before choosing what to carry forward for [AI Jam 4](https://itch.io/jam/ai-jam-4).

Horizon Charge turns it into speed: fly fast enough to sustain an ion craft’s electrical charge while threading authored tower formations. Charge Knights treats it as a battlefield command, with a formation assembled before each wave and surviving fighters carrying forward. Charge Grid explores the infrastructure meaning through fuel routes, generation types, and a civic charge target. Plug & Prosper makes it tactile: drag device cables into matching receptacles, stack adapters, and keep a small charging shop moving.

The point is not to polish four games in parallel, but to compare four very different loops—speedrunning, formation tactics, infrastructure management, and a hands-on routing puzzle. Charge Grid is still my probable entry, although I am not locking the choice yet.

![A neon ion craft flying along a curved planetary corridor between dark monolithic towers, with charge, distance, and velocity instruments around the screen.](../media/charge-grid-2026-08-01-four-directions-for-the-jam/horizon-charge.png)

![Two opposing medieval formations facing across a storybook battlefield while the player recruits a left flank before sounding the charge.](../media/charge-grid-2026-08-01-four-directions-for-the-jam/charge-knights.png)

![An isometric Charge Grid board with hand-crank, coal, solar, wind, and storage infrastructure arranged among deposits, roads, fields, and houses.](../media/charge-grid-2026-08-01-four-directions-for-the-jam/charge-grid.png)

![A cheerful charging-shop workbench where a Pocket Pal’s cable is connected through a visible stack of shape adapters while its patience and charge rise.](../media/charge-grid-2026-08-01-four-directions-for-the-jam/plug-and-prosper.png)
